comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INTERMITTENCY PROVEN — same tree, two runs, different outcomes. This is the order-dependence, measured.

Three full default-selection runs, all `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6 --dist
worksteal`:

  1. e3cd tree 25f5146dc0, agent's run  -> 1 FAILED (test_success_telemetry_survives_an_empty_usage_dict),
                                           9130 passed
  2. CLEAN main 6cdd4b00d9, no e3cd     -> 0 failed, 9219 passed, exit 0
  3. e3cd tree 25f5146dc0, UNCHANGED, re-run -> 0 failed, 9139 passed, exit 0

Run 3 is the decisive one: the SAME TREE that failed in run 1 passes on re-run with nothing changed.
So the failure is NOT caused by the e3cd change, and it is NOT deterministic. `--dist worksteal`
assigns tests to workers nondeterministically, so whether a given worker executes
`configure_logging()` before a caplog-asserting test varies run to run.

WHY RUN 2 PASSING IS NOT EVIDENCE THE BUG IS ABSENT — and this is the part worth carrying to 9ac2:
the poisoning may well have occurred in run 2 and simply produced no red. A void caplog assertion
only fails if it is written positively (`any(...)` raises AssertionError, `next(...)` raises
StopIteration). A negative assertion (`assert not caplog.records`) passes VACUOUSLY against the empty
list. So a green run is consistent with both "no poisoning" and "poisoning happened and every affected
assertion was the silent kind". The suite cannot distinguish them, which is exactly 9ac2's point.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET: the poisoner is real and proven on clean main (`configure_logging()` flips
`logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` True -> False process-globally, never restored), but the RED
symptom is intermittent, so "the suite is green" must not be used as evidence that this is fixed. A fix
needs the deterministic guard, not a passing run.

e3cd was pushed to Gerrit as change 1263 on this basis: its own gates are clean (lint 0, typecheck 0)
and its tree passes the full suite; the one observed failure is this pre-existing intermittent flake,
not a regression it introduced.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FIXED in commit 590e0e070f (not pushed). configure_logging() no longer touches propagate.

MECHANISM CORRECTION, measured on this tree with pytest 9.1.1. The "poisons the rest of the
process" premise is only partly right. `_pytest.logging.catching_logs.__enter__` attaches the
capture handler to every logger that is ALREADY non-propagating, so a logger poisoned before a
test phase starts IS still captured. Its own source comment records the remaining hole: "will
miss loggers that *become* non-propagating after the `__enter__`". So the void window is ONE
TEST PHASE wide - the test that calls configure_logging() mid-capture - not process-wide. That
is exactly the shape of the two-test probe on the ticket (test_b calls configure_logging() then
asserts, inside its own phase), and it is why a full instrumented run finds zero downstream
victims. The window is still silent, and the mitigation is an internal detail of _pytest.logging
rather than a contract, so removing the mutation is still the right fix.

WHY REMOVAL IS SAFE FOR THE DOUBLE-LOGGING AC. The docstring justified propagate=False as "so
records do not double-log through uvicorn/root". uvicorn configures only the uvicorn.* loggers
and adds NO root handler (verified: the only propagate mutations in site-packages are
uvicorn/config.py on uvicorn.access and uvicorn/workers.py on uvicorn.*), so a propagated rebar.*
record finds no second sink. The marker-guarded handler is installed at most once, which is the
only duplication this function can itself cause. test_configure_logging_is_idempotent now asserts
that on the STREAM - it emits a probe line and asserts exactly one occurrence in stdout - instead
of inferring single-emission from the handler list.

MUTATION EVIDENCE BOTH DIRECTIONS. With the fix: 4 passed (the three existing configure_logging
tests plus the new pin). Reintroducing `lg.propagate = False` after `lg.setLevel(level)`:
test_configure_logging_leaves_rebar_log_propagation_intact FAILS ("assert False is True" on
`logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate`), the other 3 stay green.

Gates by exit code: make lint 0, make typecheck 0 (mypy, 416 files).

NOT pushed to Gerrit, ticket left in_progress, per operator instruction.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

A full default-selection run (`make test`) fails with ONE test, which passes in isolation:

    FAILED tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py::test_success_telemetry_survives_an_empty_usage_dict
      - StopIteration
      at: line = next(r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records if "llm call [" in r.getMessage())

Isolated: `pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` -> 12 passed. Order-dependent, not a defect
in the test's own subject.

## Proven mechanism (clean tree, no other changes applied)

`src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:120 configure_logging()` does, at lines 145-146:

    lg = logging.getLogger("rebar")
    lg.setLevel(level)
    lg.propagate = False

`propagate = False` on the shared `rebar` parent logger is PROCESS-GLOBAL and is never restored.
pytest's `caplog` captures via a handler on the ROOT logger, so once propagation is off no
`rebar.*` record can reach it again. Every subsequent caplog assertion silently sees zero records.

Reproduced directly on a CLEAN checkout (changes stashed), two tests in one file:

    def test_a_baseline(caplog):                 # PASSES
        with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO): _emit()
        assert any("llm call [" in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)

    def test_b_after_configure_logging(caplog):  # FAILS: assert False
        from rebar.review_bot.config import configure_logging
        configure_logging()
        with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO): _emit()
        assert any("llm call [" in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)

Result: `1 failed, 1 passed`. The only difference is the `configure_logging()` call.
`caplog.at_level()` does not help - it adjusts levels, not propagation.

Two entry points reach it: `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1288` calls it directly, and
`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:202` calls it at MODULE IMPORT time (so merely importing the app
poisons the process; that path is inert in this checkout only because `fastapi` is absent).

## Why this matters beyond one red test

The failure is silent and non-local: it does not point at `configure_logging`, it points at an
unrelated victim whose position in the run order falls after the poisoning. Any future caplog
assertion on a `rebar.*` logger is one ordering change away from the same mystery, and the
affected assertions provide NO coverage in a full run while appearing green in isolation.

## Suggested direction (not implemented)

`propagate = False` exists to stop double-logging through uvicorn/root in the container. Options:
attach the handler without disabling propagation and rely on the existing marker guard to avoid
duplicates; make the propagation change conditional on actually running under uvicorn; or add an
autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py` that snapshots and restores the `rebar` logger's
`level`/`propagate`/`handlers` around every test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A caplog-based assertion on a `rebar.*` logger still captures records after
      `configure_logging()` has run in the same process, pinned by a test that fails before the fix.
- [ ] The double-logging that `propagate=False` was introduced to prevent is still prevented; the
      existing `test_configure_logging_emits_rebar_info_to_stdout` and
      `test_configure_logging_is_idempotent` stay green.
- [ ] `make test` (default selection) is green by exit code with no order-dependent failure.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code.
compiled_state.title: configure_logging() sets propagate=False on the shared 'rebar' logger, silently breaking every later caplog test in the process
